title: CLI: Support addon-vitest setup when --skip-install is passed
body:
Closes #32377

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

Run @storybook/addon-vitest's and @storybook/addon-a11y's postinstall even with --skip-install during `init`. Bundle and call the addon's postinstall directly during init, avoiding runtime resolution failures when deps aren’t installed.

**Use the package export instead of direct source import.**

This imports the vitest postinstall directly from source, bypassing the public package export. Since `@storybook/addon-vitest/postinstall` is explicitly exported in the package.json, use that instead:

```typescript
import addonVitestPostinstall from '@storybook/addon-vitest/postinstall';
```

The current deep relative path (`../../../../addons/vitest/src/postinstall`) is fragile and will break if the directory structure changes. Using the package export ensures:
- Compatibility with the built/distributed version
- Resilience to internal restructuring
- Consistency with the package's intended API

**Dynamic template import with .txt extension will fail at runtime in Node.js.**

The recent refactoring changed template files to `.txt` extension, but `await import(\`../templates/${name}\`)` cannot import `.txt` files as ES modules in Node.js—it throws `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION`. This breaks the postinstall hook when called with `.txt` filenames (e.g., `'vitest.workspace.template.txt'`).

Use `fs.readFile()` with `new URL()` to load templates as plain text instead:
```javascript
const templatePath = new URL(`../templates/${name}`, import.meta.url);
const template = await fs.readFile(templatePath, 'utf8');
```

Alternatively, revert template files to `.js` extension with default exports, or use `import.meta.glob()` for eager static imports.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/addons/vitest/src/updateVitestFile.ts` around lines 3 - 8, The
loadTemplate function currently uses dynamic ESM import (await
import(`../templates/${name}`)) which fails for .txt template files; replace the
dynamic import with reading the template file as text using fs.readFile and a
URL built from import.meta.url (e.g., construct templatePath via new
URL(`../templates/${name}`, import.meta.url) and await fs.readFile(templatePath,
'utf8')) so loadTemplate returns the plain text template; update references to
templateModule/default to use the read string, and add a minimal fs import if
missing.
```

</details>

**Address inconsistency: Other package manager proxies lack `useRemotePkg` support**

The PNPMProxy implementation adds `useRemotePkg` support, but NPMProxy, Yarn1Proxy, and Yarn2Proxy do not have equivalent implementations. This creates an inconsistency across package managers:

- **NPMProxy**: `runPackageCommand` accepts only basic options and `args` (no `useRemotePkg`)
- **Yarn1Proxy**: `runPackageCommand` accepts only `args` and options (no `useRemotePkg`)
- **Yarn2Proxy**: `runPackageCommand` accepts only `args` and options (no `useRemotePkg`)

Either add `useRemotePkg` support to all proxies, or remove it from PNPMProxy to maintain consistency across the codebase.
